name: Chicago Community Bond Fund
mission: The Chicago Community Bond Fund (CCBF) pays bond for people charged with crimes in Cook County, Illinois. Through a revolving fund, CCBF supports individuals whose communities cannot afford to pay the bonds themselves and who have been impacted by structural violence.
theoryOfChange: By paying bond, CCBF restores the presumption of innocence before trial and enables recipients to remain free while fighting their cases. People free on bond have better case outcomes than people are locked up.

rich_narrative.summary: The Chicago Community Bond Fund operates a revolving fund to <cite id="3">pay bond for individuals in Cook County</cite> who cannot afford it, protecting individuals from pretrial detention. The main limiting factor for the organization is financial sustainability. In FY2024, the charity reported <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $510,635</cite>, reflecting a steep revenue decline from <cite id="2">$751,883 in FY2023</cite> and <cite id="2">$897,686 in FY2022</cite>. Moreover, the organization's spending significantly exceeded its earnings, with <cite id="1">expenses reaching 5.0x total revenue</cite> ($2,539,788 in spending against $510,635 in revenue). While <cite id="1">Charity Navigator awards the organization an overall score of 96/100</cite> and notes strong fundraising efficiency with <cite id="1">$0.11 spent to raise $1</cite>, the substantial deficit poses long-term continuity concerns. Additionally, as a general legal advocacy group, the organization has low specific alignment for traditional Islamic giving, and its offerings are strictly sadaqah-eligible.
